facts.statement: Diandongpetalichthys was an extinct placoderm that lived in China during the Early Devonian period.
facts.quote: Diandongpetalichthys liaojiaoshanensis is an extinct petalichthyid placoderm from the Early Devonian of China.

facts.statement: Fossils of Diandongpetalichthys include one complete skull roof, several incomplete skull roofs, parts of the trunk shield, and spines.
facts.quote: Several specimens, in the forms of one complete and several incomplete skull roofs, disarticulated portions of the trunk shield, and spines, are known

facts.statement: The fossils were found in the non-marine Xishancun Formation at Liaojiaoshan Hill in Qujing, Yunnan.
facts.quote: found in the Devonian aged Liaojiaoshan Hill of Qujing, Yunnan, a non-marine portion of the Xishancun Formation, in the Cuifengshan Group.

facts.statement: Based on better-preserved specimens showing features similar to primitive arthrodires, Diandongpetalichthys is now classified as a basal member of the order Petalichthyida.
facts.quote: D. liaojiaoshanensis is now regarded as a basal petalichthyid.

facts.statement: Diandongpetalichthys lived during the Lochkovian stage, between 419.62 and 413.02 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Lochkovian to Lochkovian (419.62 to 413.02 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The species was described by P'an and Wang in 1978.
rejected.quote: Diandongpetalichthys liaojiaoshanensis is an extinct petalichthyid placoderm from the Early Devonian of China.
